text:
Anya: quick sync — here's the weekly GPU capacity snapshot i pulled, flagged items at the bottom. high-level: US-EAST tight on p4x16s for promo traffic, EU-WEST has spare T4s but not compatible with recent quantized weights, APAC is fragile due to egress caps.
Mike: can you paste the numbers?
Anya: sure — raw: 
- US-EAST (cluster-orion): available p4x16: 18 nodes (144 GPUs), projected burn next 7d: 1728 GPU-hours/day, expected peak day: 2200 GPU-hours (promo + batch).
- EU-WEST (cluster-borealis): available t4s: 120 GPUs, v100-equivalent: ~60 (via burst), projected burn: 800 GPU-hours/day, peak: 1100 GPU-hours.
- APAC (cluster-tide): mixed A10s + preemptible p4s: 42 GPUs total, projected burn: 420 GPU-hours/day, peak: 680 (night/marketing).
Oliver: numbers look right vs telemetry. what's the headroom margin?
Anya: headroom (buffer after SLO reserve): US-EAST: ~9% (low), EU-WEST: ~36%, APAC: ~12%. note: US-EAST includes 2 scheduled maintenance windows this week that will reduce available by ~8 GPUs for 4h each.
Sam: root cause on the US-EAST squeeze — is it demand spike or allocation leak?
Anya: mix: 60% demand spike from new partner integration + 25% long-lived batch jobs not adhering to soft-limits. we've throttled some batch but need long-term fix.
Li: infra-bot: alert created for orion-high-burn (id: #INC-9123).
infra-bot: automated message — created incident INC-9123, paging oncall.
Mike: options? can we shift some real-time traffic to eu-west during overlap windows? latency penalty ~40-70ms but may be acceptable for non-critical customers.
Anya: propose policy: route non-SLA routes to EU-WEST during <14:00-18:00 UTC for next 3 days. also bump preemptible ratio in APAC from 30% -> 50% for weekend burst.
Oliver: do we have network egress budget to cross-route? APAC -> EU is fine, US->EU egress for traffic to customers in NA would be bad. need legal check for data residency for partner X.
Sam: cost impact of routing to EU? rough calc?
Anya: rough delta: moving 200 GPU-hours/day from US to EU adds ~0.02 $/token-equivalent in egress + spot diff ~+$240/day. still cheaper than emergency on-demand p4x16 spin-up (~+$1.2k/day).
Li: noted. also APAC preemptible increase risk: preempt rate historically ~9% during working hours, jumps to ~18% overnight if cloud provider reclaims. implication: we need faster reconnect/retry logic for streaming sessions.
Mike: action items: 
- Anya -> implement routing rule for non-SLA routes (owner: Anya) by EOD today.
- Oliver -> confirm data residency constraints for Partner X by EOD (owner: Oliver).
- Sam -> patch batch job soft-limits and add circuit-breaker to long-lived jobs (owner: Sam) by tomorrow noon.
- Li -> add temporary alert thresholds for p4x16 saturation in orion (owner: Li) and increase retention on burn traces for 72h.
Anya: also scheduling two mitigations if routes don't help: 1) short-term reserved capacity purchase for 72h (3 p4x16 nodes) — ops cost ~+$6k; 2) canary lightweight quantized model rollout to reduce GPU time ~12% on latency-sensitive endpoints (needs approvals).
Oliver: +1 on quantized canary, will prep rollout plan but need QE signoff.
Mike: timeline for visibility — we'll re-evaluate in 24h, set check-in at 3022110456. if still >85% saturation we'll execute reserved capacity.
Anya: sounds good. attaching snippet of the command I used to derive headroom: 
```
# calculate headroom per cluster
python infra/tools/forecast.py --cluster orion --window 7d --percentile 95 --output json
```
Sam: quick note — batch jobs are being migrated this week, some old workers still have legacy image; i'll triage which ones to evict first.
Li: added runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/capacity-scaling and pinned INC-9123 in incidents channel.
Mike: thanks all — short meeting later if numbers move. :thumbsup:
